title: Prepositions of Time: In, On, At
description: Master the pyramid of time prepositions: AT (specific), ON (days/dates), and IN (long periods).
objectives: Apply 'AT' for precise clock times, night, and specific points in time
Apply 'ON' for days of the week, dates, and specific day parts (on Friday night)
Apply 'IN' for months, years, seasons, centuries, and parts of the day (in the morning)

sections.title: The In / On / At Pyramid of Time
sections.content:
Think of time prepositions as an **inverted pyramid** that moves from the broadest, longest time periods down to the most specific points in time:

### 1. IN (Broad / Long Periods)
- **Parts of the day**: *in the morning*, *in the afternoon*, *in the evening*.
- **Months**: *in July*, *in December*.
- **Seasons**: *in summer*, *in winter*.
- **Years**: *in 2026*, *in 1947*.
- **Centuries**: *in the 21st century*.

### 2. ON (Days & Dates)
- **Days of the week**: *on Monday*, *on Friday*.
- **Specific dates**: *on the 14th of August*, *on May 5th*.
- **Day + part of day**: *on Friday morning*, *on Sunday evening*.
- **Holidays with 'Day'**: *on Independence Day*, *on Eid day*.

### 3. AT (Specific Precise Points)
- **Exact clock times**: *at 5:00 PM*, *at half past two*.
- **Fixed points**: *at noon*, *at midnight*, *at sunset*.
- **Special expressions**: *at night*, *at the weekend* (UK).

callouts.title: The Day + Part of Day Exception
callouts.text: Even though we say *in the morning*, if you add a specific day, **ON wins**: say **on Monday morning** (never *in Monday morning*)!

callouts.title: Weekend: At vs. On
callouts.text: In British English, say **at the weekend**. In American English, say **on the weekend**. Both are understood globally.

sections.title: Lesson Summary
summaryPoints: AT = specific precise times (at 5:00, at noon, at midnight, at night).
ON = days and dates (on Monday, on the 14th of August, on Friday night).
IN = longer periods (in July, in 2026, in summer, in the morning).
Day + part of day: 'ON' always wins (on Monday morning).
